Operation Cast Lead

Military Operation · 2008-12-27 · 22-day Israeli military operation in Gaza Strip

22 days

Location, thenGaza Strip, Gaza, Hamas-governed Gaza Strip under Israeli blockade since 2007
Location, nowGaza Strip, Under Israeli blockade and occupation; governed by Hamas, Ongoing blockade since 2007; reconstruction incomplete
PerpetratorsIsrael Defense Forces; Israeli Air Force; Ground forces and naval units
ClassificationWar Crimes; Crimes Against Humanity (UN Goldstone Report)

Summary

Operation Cast Lead began at 11:30 AM on December 27, 2008, when Israeli F-16 fighter jets and Apache helicopters simultaneously struck over 100 pre-planned targets across Gaza within 220 seconds. The opening attacks hit police stations—including during a graduation ceremony for new officers, killing 99 police personnel—government buildings, and Hamas infrastructure. By the end of the first day, at least 230 Palestinians were killed.

The aerial bombardment continued for seven days before Israeli ground forces invaded Gaza from the north and east on January 3, 2009. The navy simultaneously shelled from offshore. Over 22 days, Israeli forces conducted what the UN investigation described as a deliberately disproportionate attack designed to punish, humiliate and terrorize a civilian population. The operation involved widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure including hospitals, schools, mosques, United Nations facilities, water installations, and sewage treatment plants.

Multiple incidents documented by the UN mission and human rights organizations revealed patterns of violations: the Samouni family massacre where soldiers forced approximately 100 civilians into a building then shelled it killing 21; the Al-Daya family airstrike killing 22 civilians; several cases where soldiers shot civilians carrying white flags; and extensive use of white phosphorus munitions in densely populated areas. The Palestinian Centre for Human Rights documented 1,419 Palestinian deaths including 1,167 civilians, while B'Tselem reported 1,385 killed including 762 noncombatants and 318 minors.

Timeline

2008-11-04 00:00:00 Israeli raid breaks ceasefireIsrael launches cross-border raid into Gaza to destroy tunnel. Multiple sources report this broke the six-month ceasefire. Hamas responds with rocket fire, ending truce. — UN Documentation
November–December 2008 Escalating violenceIncreasing rocket fire from Gaza and Israeli strikes. Over 100 rockets fired in 24 hours before operation begins. Multiple escalations and failed ceasefire attempts. — UN OCHA Monthly Reports
2008-12-27 11:30:00 Operation begins – massive airstrikesIsraeli F-16s and Apache helicopters strike 100+ targets in 220 seconds. Police headquarters hit during graduation ceremony; 99 police officers and 9 civilians killed. By end of first day, 230 Palestinians dead. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 28-35
27 Dec 2008 – 3 Jan 2009 Week of aerial bombardmentContinuous airstrikes hit government buildings, police stations, mosques, homes, infrastructure. Israeli navy shells from offshore. White phosphorus used in populated areas. Hundreds killed. — Amnesty International
2009-01-03 00:00:00 Ground invasion beginsIsraeli ground forces invade Gaza from north and east. Tanks and infantry enter Beit Lahiya and Beit Hanoun. Gaza effectively bisected. Tens of thousands flee their homes. — UN OCHA Situation Reports
4–5 January 2009 Samouni family massacreIsraeli soldiers ordered approximately 100 members of Samouni family into single building in Zaytoun area. On January 5, shelling killed 21 civilians. Survivors trapped with dead for days. Red Cross denied access. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 726-756
2009-01-06 00:00:00 Al-Daya family massacreIsraeli F-16 fires missile at home of Al-Daya family in Zaytoun neighborhood. 22 family members killed, mostly women and children. Israeli military later admitted house struck by mistake. — UN OCHA Report
2009-01-07 00:00:00 White flag' killings documentedMultiple incidents where Israeli soldiers killed Palestinians fleeing while carrying white flags. Majda and Rayya Hajjaj (aged 37 and 65) shot while fleeing. UN mission documented 7 such incidents. — HRW Report 'White Flag Deaths'
2009-01-15 00:00:00 UNRWA compound attackedUN Relief and Works Agency compound in Gaza City shelled with high explosive and white phosphorus. 600-700 civilians sheltering there. Attack continued for hours despite Israeli forces being alerted to risks. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 39
2009-01-15 00:00:00 Al-Quds Hospital attackedIsraeli forces directly attacked al-Quds hospital in Gaza City and adjacent ambulance depot. White phosphorus used. Pattern of attacks on medical facilities documented throughout operation. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 39
2009-01-18 00:00:00 Ceasefire declaredUnder enormous international pressure, Israel declares unilateral ceasefire and withdraws forces. Palestinian armed groups follow with separate ceasefire. No formal agreement reached. — UN Security Council Records
2009-04-03 00:00:00 UN Fact-Finding Mission establishedUN Human Rights Council establishes Fact-Finding Mission led by Justice Richard Goldstone to investigate possible violations of international law by all parties during conflict. — UN Human Rights Council Resolution
2009-09-15 00:00:00 Goldstone Report releasedUN mission releases 575-page report documenting alleged war crimes by Israeli military and Palestinian armed groups. Report finds evidence of deliberately disproportionate attacks on civilians. — UN Goldstone Report (Full Text)
2009-10-16 00:00:00 UN Human Rights Council endorses reportHuman Rights Council endorses Goldstone Report by vote of 25 to 6, with 11 abstentions. Recommends referral to Security Council and potentially International Criminal Court. — UN HRC Resolution

Testimony

Justice Richard GoldstoneThe Mission found that the operations were carefully planned in all their phases — what occurred in just over three weeks at the end of 2008 and the beginning of 2009 was a deliberately disproportionate attack designed to punish, humiliate and terrorize a civilian population. — UN Goldstone Report Press Conference, 15 September 2009
Ateya al-SamouniTestified to UN mission: soldiers ordered all of us into one house, around 100 people, mostly women and children. They kept us there all day and night. The next morning they started shelling the house. My mother was killed instantly. We were trapped with the dead and dying for three days before ambulances could reach us. Lost 21 family members. — UN Goldstone Report testimony, June 2009
Dr. Khalid EshkuntanaTestified about treating white phosphorus injuries: We saw burns we had never seen before. The phosphorus continues to burn even inside the body. We had no experience treating such weapons. Many patients died from these burns. — Amnesty International interviews, January 2009
John DugardIn statement to UN: Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a gross and systematic violation of the Fourth Geneva Convention. The attack was not simply an act of war, but a sustained and brutal assault on a civilian population that had been living under siege for 18 months. — UN Human Rights Council statement, March 2009
Breaking the SilenceAnonymous soldier testimony: The commanders made it clear — our lives come first, and then moral considerations. We were told that if we see any person, even if they seem innocent, if we feel threatened, we shoot. The destruction was unimaginable. We destroyed so many houses that served no military purpose. — Breaking the Silence testimonies, July 2009
International Committee of the Red CrossICRC issued rare public criticism: The Israeli military failed to meet its obligation under international humanitarian law to care for and evacuate the wounded. The ICRC views the delay in allowing rescue services access as unacceptable. Regarding Samouni family incident. — ICRC Press Release, 8 January 2009
Amnesty InternationalIn detailed report: Israeli forces carried out direct attacks against civilians and civilian objects in Gaza, and attacks which were disproportionate or indiscriminate, failing to distinguish between legitimate military targets and civilian objects. Many of the attacks involved the use of white phosphorus and other weapons supplied by the USA. — Amnesty Report 'Operation Cast Lead: 22 days of death and destruction', July 2009
Human Rights WatchDocumented white flag killings: In seven cases documented by Human Rights Watch, Israeli forces in Gaza attacked groups of people who were trying to convey their civilian status by waving white flags. The attacks killed 11 civilians. — HRW Report, August 2009

War crimes

Samouni Family MassacreIsraeli soldiers forced approximately 100 members of Samouni family into single building in Zaytoun area, held them 24 hours, then shelled building killing 21 civilians. Survivors trapped with dead for days; ambulances prevented from accessing area. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 726-756
Al-Daya Family AirstrikeF-16 missile strike on Al-Daya family home killed 22 civilians, mostly women and children. Israeli military later admitted house struck by mistake. UN mission found 'substantial failure of due diligence'. — UN OCHA Documentation
White Flag KillingsIsraeli soldiers killed at least 11 Palestinian civilians who were fleeing while carrying white flags. Documented cases include killing of two women (Majda and Rayya Hajjaj, aged 37 and 65). — Human Rights Watch Report
White Phosphorus in Populated AreasIsraeli forces used white phosphorus—illegal when used in populated areas—in attacks on two hospitals (Al-Quds, Al-Wafa), UN compound in Gaza City, and densely populated residential areas. — Amnesty International Report
Attacks on Medical and UN FacilitiesDirect attacks on protected sites including al-Quds hospital, al-Wafa hospital, UNRWA compound sheltering 600-700 civilians. Attacks continued despite clear marking and notification to Israeli forces. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 39
Destruction of Civilian InfrastructureSystematic destruction of flour mills, water installations, sewage treatment plants with no military justification. El-Bader flour mill—only functioning mill in Gaza—destroyed. 268 businesses completely destroyed. — UN Goldstone Report, para. 50
Deliberately Disproportionate ForceUN mission concluded operations were carefully planned in all phases with patterns indicating deliberate targeting of civilians. Described as a deliberately disproportionate attack designed to punish, humiliate and terrorize civilian population. — UN Goldstone Report, Executive Summary
Palestinian Rocket Attacks (War Crime)Palestinian armed groups fired over 900 rockets and mortars into Israel during operation, killing 3 Israeli civilians. Goldstone Report concluded these were indiscriminate attacks constituting war crimes. — UN Goldstone Report

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention — Israeli ForcesArticle 27 (Protected Persons): Samouni massacre, white flag killings, and other deliberate attacks on civilians violated core protections.
Customary IHL ViolationsDistinction: Attacks on Samouni family, Al-Daya family, white flag carriers violated fundamental principle of distinction between civilians and combatants.
UN Goldstone Report Findings (September 2009)War Crimes: Report found evidence Israeli forces committed actions amounting to war crimes, including wilful killing and extensive destruction of property not justified by military necessity.
Human Rights Law ViolationsRight to Life (ICCPR Article 6): Deliberate killings of civilians violated right to life. Al-Daya case specifically found to violate Article 6.
Fourth Geneva Convention — Israeli ForcesArticle 33 (Collective Punishments): UN mission found operation designed to punish, humiliate and terrorize Gaza's civilian population — textbook collective punishment.
Customary IHL ViolationsProportionality: UN mission found deliberately disproportionate force throughout operation.
UN Goldstone Report Findings (September 2009)Crimes Against Humanity: Report concluded Israeli actions may amount to crimes against humanity — deliberately disproportionate attack designed to punish, humiliate and terrorize civilian population.
Human Rights Law ViolationsRight to Adequate Housing: Destruction of 3,540 homes, leaving 20,000+ homeless, violated right to adequate housing under ICESCR.
Fourth Geneva Convention — Israeli ForcesArticle 53 (Destruction of Property): Destruction of flour mills, water systems, 3,540+ homes lacked military necessity.
Customary IHL ViolationsPrecautions in Attack: Attacks on UNRWA compound and hospitals continued after notification violated precautionary requirements.
UN Goldstone Report Findings (September 2009)Palestinian War Crimes: Report also found Palestinian armed groups committed war crimes through indiscriminate rocket attacks on Israeli civilians.
Human Rights Law ViolationsRight to Health: Attacks on hospitals, medical facilities, destruction of health infrastructure violated right to health.
Fourth Geneva Convention — Israeli ForcesArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): Wilful killing, extensive destruction not justified by military necessity. Multiple documented incidents meet this threshold.
Customary IHL ViolationsProtected Objects: Direct attacks on Al-Quds hospital, UNRWA compound violated their protected status.
UN Goldstone Report Findings (September 2009)Accountability: Recommended both parties conduct good faith investigations within 6 months; if not, Security Council should refer situation to International Criminal Court.
Human Rights Law ViolationsRights of the Child: 333 children killed; attacks on schools; targeting of civilian areas violated Convention on Rights of the Child.

Commanders

1945–present Ehud OlmertAuthorized Operation Cast Lead and made key policy decisions during offensive. Later stated operation was necessary but expressed regret over civilian casualties. In 2015 convicted of corruption in unrelated case.
1942–present Ehud BarakOversaw planning and execution of military operations. Defended operation as proportionate response to rocket fire.
1954–present Gabi AshkenaziTop military commander during operation. Responsible for operational planning and execution. Maintained operation was conducted according to international law.
1962–present Ismail HaniyehHamas political leader during operation. Continued to authorize rocket attacks into Israel. Rejected ceasefire offers during operation.
1938–present Justice Richard GoldstoneLed UN investigation into Operation Cast Lead. Former Constitutional Court Justice of South Africa and Chief Prosecutor for International Criminal Tribunals.
